title: Goldleaf Financial — Infosec Evidence Compilation for Dedicated POC
summary: This packet aggregates the artifacts and narrative needed for Goldleaf Financial's Dedicated POC infosec review. It covers control mappings (SOC2/ISO-informative), concrete evidence files, short test results, and a compact remediation plan for outstanding items discovered during the 2025-11 through 2026-01 evidence collection window. The goal: enable Goldleaf security reviewers and auditors to validate Redwood's Dedicated deployment surface and operational controls for a finance-regulated POC.
scope: Scope: Dedicated POC environment provisioned in us-east-2 using Redwood Dedicated reserved pool (single-tenant GPU nodes) with VPC peering to Goldleaf dev VPC. Data processed during the POC consisted of synthetic finance records and obfuscated customer strings. Excluded: production customer data, PCI workloads. Timeline: provisioning 2025-11-04, workshop and evidence handover 2025-11-05 to 2026-01-15.

control_mappings:
SOC2-like control mapping (informative):
- CC6.1 Logical access controls -> evidence: iam-access-audit-2025-12.csv, runbook for access provisioning.
- CC7.1 Encryption of data in transit and at rest -> evidence: kms-config-snapshot.txt, tls-certs-rotation.txt, sbom and container runtime TLS configs.
- CC8.3 Change management -> evidence: terraform commits and change log; PR links in linked_artifacts.
- CC5.2 System operations -> evidence: monitoring-dash-2025-12.png, runbook-dedicated-incident-play.md.
- ISO-like references: A.9 (access control), A.10 (cryptography), A.12 (operations security) mapped to the same artifacts.
Notes: This mapping is a POC-level complement, not a full SOC2 audit deliverable. For formal audits we recommend client-led audit scope creation and Redwood-attested control descriptions.
technical_notes:
Key technical decisions and test outcomes: 
- Encryption: All POC data stored on attached NVMe volumes encrypted using customer-managed KMS CMKs (Goldleaf provided; snapshot in kms-config-snapshot.txt). Envelope encryption performed by Redwood runtime with ephemeral per-request data keys.
- Network: VPC peering and strict egress ACLs used. Test outbound whitelist included: OS package repos and NTP. egress-scan demonstrates no unexpected external flows.
- Access & IAM: Role-based access granted via SCIM-integrated IdP for Goldleaf engineers; Redwood engineers had time-bound, logged jumpbox access. Access audit shows two developer accounts with >90-day inactivity flagged for removal.
- Secrets: HSM integration simulated; production HSM options available. For POC we used customer KMS with KMS logs retained 90 days.
- Runtime images: Images are built from pinned base images; SBOMs included. No high severity CVEs were present in runtime libs for POC inputs; medium/low CVEs and mitigation plans are in sbom-dedicated-2025-11.json.
- Observability: Traces redact prompt content and only surface request metadata to logging. Sample trace shows hashed prompt identifiers only.
- Pen test: Scoped external network and web-facing surface. Pentest summary lists 4 low findings (informational/config recommendations) and one medium (incomplete tokenization in a test harness) which was mitigated and retested.
- Data purge: Automated task removed POC artifacts and tested deletion produced cryptographic deletion confirmation entries recorded in purge-log-2025-12-20.csv.
workshop_notes:
2025-11-05 onsite workshop (recording linked). Key outcomes: 
- Goldleaf required dedicated tenancy and a customer-managed KMS which was accepted and implemented.
- Goldleaf wanted proof of access separation — we agreed to provide an expanded IAM report and time-limited jumpbox logs for the final handover.
- Goldleaf security asked for an expanded retention matrix; action: provide per-artifact retention policy in 2 business days (ACTION-1).
- SRE presented incident-play steps and Goldleaf asked for a tabletop on a model-exfiltration scenario; action: schedule tabletop in Jan 2026 (ACTION-2).
- Agreement that PII would not be used in the POC; Goldleaf security will provide a redaction checklist for future runs.
Notes: meeting minutes and Q&A compiled in goldleaf-poc-workshop-notes.docx (artifact).

conclusion_and_next_steps: Conclusion: The Dedicated POC met Goldleaf's initial architectural and operational controls with a small set of actionable items (tabletop exercise scheduling and expanded IAM artifact delivery). The artifacts included here provide a compact evidentiary trail suitable for initial security evaluation. Next steps: (1) complete ACTION-2 tabletop and produce exercise report, (2) finalize and hand over the IAM evidence bundle, (3) plan formal audit scoping if Goldleaf moves to procurement. For procurement support, prepare a SOC2-friendly control narrative and a longer retention evidence set (ask: Goldleaf to confirm audit timeline).
